outcome_algebra.scan_summary: For certificate prefix P, summarize S(P)=(D,fr,f,u,t,q): D is the finite set of defined rejecting defects keyed by (anchor_position,guard_rank); fr=min(D) or none; f is semantic fail_seen from schema-complete semantically admissible H_d evidence; u is UNKNOWN-barrier-seen; t is the last-row boundary interface needed to evaluate G_order/G_chain against an appended row; q is the terminal monotone q state when defined.
outcome_algebra.diagnostic_axis: VALID iff D is empty; otherwise INVALID(fr). INVALID is diagnostic only and does not erase semantic evidence.
outcome_algebra.semantic_axis: FAIL if f=true; else UNKNOWN if u=true; else PASS if terminal q has b&r&f&s=true; else UNRESOLVED. This axis is total for every scanned prefix once undefined row-local operands are isolated by G_schema.
outcome_algebra.total_outcome: Omega(P)=(diagnostic_axis,semantic_axis,accepted), where accepted=true iff diagnostic_axis=VALID and semantic_axis=PASS. Thus INVALID+FAIL, INVALID+UNKNOWN, INVALID+PASS and INVALID+UNRESOLVED remain representable without flattening away evidence; any flat display label INVALID must still retain the semantic component in the durable record.
outcome_algebra.precedence: Semantic FAIL outranks UNKNOWN/PASS/UNRESOLVED only within the semantic axis. INVALID never semantically outranks FAIL; it blocks acceptance on the orthogonal diagnostic axis.

prefix_extension_composition.definition: Let P have n input rows and append suffix X without editing positions 1..n. New unary defects in X and all new cross-boundary G_order/G_chain defects anchor at positions >n (the first boundary defect anchors at n+1).
prefix_extension_composition.first_rejection_rule: If fr(P) exists, fr(P·X)=fr(P) because every new defect key has a strictly later anchor; if fr(P) is none, fr(P·X) is the lexicographic minimum of newly introduced defect keys, or none. Therefore canonical first_rejection is stable under pure prefix extension and independent of guard evaluator visitation order.
prefix_extension_composition.fail_rule: f(P·X)=f(P) OR f_new(X|t(P)); therefore once semantic FAIL evidence is observed it cannot be suppressed by any appended rows or diagnostic faults.
prefix_extension_composition.unknown_rule: u(P·X)=u(P) OR u_new(X|t(P)); UNKNOWN remains fail-closed unless FAIL is observed, in which case semantic_axis=FAIL by fixed semantic precedence.
prefix_extension_composition.boundary_rule: Only t(P), the appended row and their derived pairwise predicates are needed for new G_order/G_chain checks; old defect anchors and old semantic evidence are immutable under extension.
prefix_extension_composition.terminal_rule: q is updated only by schema-complete semantically admissible appended transitions; monotone B/R/F/S bits cannot be cleared by a valid extension, while d or UNKNOWN may newly force FAIL/UNKNOWN.

proof_obligations_satisfied: Determinism: complete defect accumulation plus a fixed total lexicographic key yields one fr for a finite input, independent of pure guard evaluation order.
Diagnostic/semantic separation: acceptance requires VALID+PASS, while INVALID never deletes f or u; C4's earlier G_class with later valid H_d is represented as (INVALID(row1,G_class),FAIL,false).
Prefix FAIL preservation: OR-composition makes f monotone under append-only extension.
Prefix first-rejection preservation: all defects created by appending have anchors after every unchanged prefix position, so an existing fr cannot be displaced.
Unknown preservation: retained UNKNOWN barrier is OR-monotone and cannot be normalized away; later FAIL remains visible and takes semantic precedence.
No false PASS: PASS requires no fail, no unknown and all B/R/F/S terminal bits; accepted additionally requires no diagnostic defects.
